newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power mixed amid mild temps, outages.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power mixed amid mild temps, outages.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mixed Friday as an unexpected outage in Florida counteracted some of the weakness resulting from the drop in weather-related demand, market sources said.
Florida Power Corp's 750 megawatt (MW) Crystal River 4 coal unit was shut early Thursday due to a transformer fire. The company said the unit would be shut for a minimum of four weeks for repairs.
At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak power prices in 16 hour blocks for Monday were fairly steady in the $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, from $19.50-20.50 on Thursday.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was still assessed at $13.00-14.00 per MWh.
In Florida, firm, peak power prices on a 16-hour schedule for Monday were talked in the $20.00-21.00 range.
Firm, peak power prices into Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) for Monday softened into the $13.75-15.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down from Thursday's trading at $16.00-17.00.
"It's mild, and it looks like it's going to last for a while. A lot of marketers seem to be pretty long too," one market source said.
Firm, off-peak power prices into TVA were talked in the $12.00-13.00 per MWh range, but no deals were confirmed done.
TVA's 1,170 MW Watts Bar nuclear power unit, in Spring City, Tenn., was expected to be back on line Friday after shutting down late Monday.
Separately, Carolina Power and Light's 880 MW Harris nuclear power plant, which tripped off line Thursday, is expected to return to service Saturday.
Also, Florida Power and Light Co's 666 MW Turkey Point 3 nuclear power unit will likely resume full production this weekend after being reduced to about 55 percent power Thursday evening.
Georgia Power's 741 MW Hatch 1 nuclear power unit remained shut but was expected to return to the grid Sunday or Monday.
Virginia Power's 781 MW Surry 1 nuclear power unit is also expected to be back on line early Saturday.
Also, Duke Power's 846 MW Oconee 2 nuclear unit, shut since last September after a steam pipe burst, will likely restart this weekend.
Oconee units 1 and 3, shut since October and each generating 846 MW, are expected to restart in February.
All three units are in Seneca, S.C.
